situation:
You are the human resources generalist at CEDAR RIDGE SANITATION, a residential and commercial waste collection company serving three counties. The director of operations (judge) has asked you to recommend how the company should handle a return-to-work decision for an injured route collector. The recommendation is yours to make and to explain.

CEDAR RIDGE acquired VALLEY HAULERS eight months ago and has not finished combining the two operations. Routes, payroll systems and dispatch desks are still separate. To secure the deal, the company assured the acquired firm's dispatchers that no one would be released during the merger year, and the plan folds those dispatchers into CEDAR RIDGE's own dispatch office at the start of next quarter.

A route collector with eleven years of service injured a shoulder lifting a commercial bin and is cleared for light duty only, with no lifting, for at least ten weeks. There is one light-duty seat available: a temporary desk in the dispatch office. That desk is also the landing spot promised to a VALLEY HAULERS dispatcher whose position closes when the offices combine.

Placing the collector at the desk returns wages this quarter and closes an open injury claim, but leaves the VALLEY HAULERS dispatcher without the landing spot next quarter. Holding the collector on full medical leave until full clearance protects that spot, and it costs the collector the route premium pay while the claim stays open and the crew works short.

The director of operations (judge) wants you to recommend one course of action, explain what it costs, and describe how you would put it in writing to the employee it affects most. The director of operations (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions. When you have finished answering, the director of operations (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the director of operations at CEDAR RIDGE SANITATION. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the human resources generalist to recommend whether the injured route collector should be placed at the temporary dispatch desk or held on medical leave until full clearance, to say plainly what that choice costs, and to describe what the company should put in writing to the employee the decision lands hardest on.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: How would you tell the employee this decision affects most what we decided and why?
What should we put in writing to that employee, and what should we say in person?
